svg.text: Figure 4.3. The router: the route decision, the output queues and round-robin selectors, and the link pipeline
v1.0 (spec/machine-spec.md §3.2, §4.6, §4.7, §4.16) — figures 4.1 and 4.2 are the block view; this is what a route block and an output do
A. A route block: one per link input, one for the loopback (injection), and on tile 0 one from C&C (§4.6)
Unicast: the result is one push enable, into this block's FIFO in the chosen output's queue set (B). Idle packets are discarded. One cycle.
Broadcast (dst 126): copies by arriving direction, s = src (64 → 0):
B. One output: its queue set, the round-robin selector, overflow, and the link pipeline (§4.7, §3.2)
to-right: injection, from-left · to-left: injection, from-right
to-up: injection, from-left, from-right, from-down · eject: loopback + all four
serve the first non-empty FIFO at or
push & full, any FIFO of the tile
From C&C: a sixth route block, deciding as an injection at tile 0 (unicast as from tile 0; a broadcast rooted at tile 0, not delivered back to C&C).
Its packets enter a "from C&C" FIFO on each of tile 0's five outputs (four links and eject), each selector gaining one input: C&C gets a fair share.
To C&C: five FIFOs (from left, right, up, down and tile 0's injection) with their own round-robin selector, one packet a cycle; every packet for dst 64 leaves here.
C&C accepts one packet a cycle (no back-pressure, §4.16); its receive FIFO is C&C's side. Address 65 is unused: the memory subsystem hangs off C&C (§7).
D. Interface of one route block and one output
link stage 3 / injection (fig 7.3) / C&C → route block
src 7, dst 7, mode 4, addr 20, payload 64; idle packets dropped
col(me) = me mod 8, row(me) = me div 8
route block → its FIFO in each output's set
one for unicast; up to five for a broadcast

• No flow control anywhere: a correct program never overflows a FIFO; the fan-in limits are §3.2's, and the schedule's queue bounds are spec/schedule.md's. Packets in one FIFO are never reordered, so one
source's packets to one destination arrive in the order sent.
junction (crossings without a dot don't connect); wedge: clocked register
Each route block decides in one cycle from src, dst and me: horizontal first by the offset table, then vertical, then eject; a broadcast
fans out by its arriving direction. Each output takes one packet a cycle from its FIFOs round-robin; a link adds three register stages,
so a hop is four cycles. A push into a full FIFO loses the packet and sets router overflow.
